rules.quote: List every `.md` file in `memory/`
rules.rule: List every .md file in the memory/ folder, excluding _PROMPT_RESTORE_MEMORY.md and MEMORY.md, when restoring memories.

rules.quote: Sort alphabetically.
rules.rule: Sort the list of memory files to restore alphabetically.

rules.quote: Read the file's full contents exactly as bytes on disk.
rules.rule: Read each memory file's full contents exactly as bytes on disk.

rules.quote: Parse the frontmatter block (between the two `---` fences) to extract:
rules.rule: Parse the frontmatter block between the two --- fences of each memory file to extract its name, description, and type.

rules.quote: Use the SAME filename as the source file.
rules.rule: Save each restored memory under the same filename as its source file.

rules.quote: Save it as a new memory entry using the auto-memory system's
rules.rule: Save each memory as a new entry using the auto-memory system's Write tool against the canonical memory path for the current project.

rules.quote: The content written must match byte-for-byte what was read
rules.rule: Ensure the written content matches the source file byte-for-byte, including frontmatter, blank lines, and trailing newline.

rules.quote: Confirm success before moving to the next file.
rules.rule: Confirm each file was saved successfully before moving to the next file.

rules.quote: After ALL memory files are saved, write `MEMORY.md` last.
rules.rule: Write MEMORY.md only after all memory files have been saved.

rules.quote: Copy its contents byte-for-byte from `memory/MEMORY.md`.
rules.rule: Copy MEMORY.md's contents byte-for-byte from memory/MEMORY.md without modification.

rules.quote: Do NOT edit content.
rules.rule: Do not edit memory content when restoring.

rules.quote: Do NOT shorten descriptions.
rules.rule: Do not shorten memory descriptions when restoring.

rules.quote:
Do NOT merge
  duplicates.
rules.rule: Do not merge duplicate memories when restoring.

rules.quote: Do NOT rename files.
rules.rule: Do not rename memory files when restoring.

rules.quote: Do NOT update dates.
rules.rule: Do not update dates in memory files when restoring.

rules.quote: Do NOT add memories that aren't in the folder.
rules.rule: Do not add memories that are not present in the memory/ folder.

rules.quote: Do NOT create a MEMORY.md from scratch — only copy the existing one.
rules.rule: Do not create MEMORY.md from scratch; only copy the existing memory/MEMORY.md.

rules.quote:
retry once, then report
  it as a discrepancy.
rules.rule: If unsure whether a save succeeded, retry once, then report it as a discrepancy.

rules.quote: Never assume success.
rules.rule: Never assume a save succeeded without confirming it.

rules.quote: Work sequentially
rules.rule: Restore memory files sequentially, one file at a time.

rules.quote: No batching.
rules.rule: Do not batch memory file reads or saves.

rules.quote: Do NOT silently skip.
rules.rule: Do not silently skip any file that fails; report it by name and exact error.

rules.quote:
name the file and
     the error exactly.
rules.rule: When a discrepancy occurs, name the file and the error exactly in the final report.

rules.quote: **Rule:** When a fix combines multiple changes (X + Z) and the result works, you have NOT identified which change actually fixed the bug. Before declaring root cause, **ablate**: revert one change at a time and verify whether the bug returns.
rules.rule: When a fix combining multiple changes works, do not declare which change fixed the bug until you have ablated: revert one change at a time and verify whether the bug returns.

rules.quote: After any multi-change fix where the bug "works now," explicitly ablate the changes that aren't obviously load-bearing.
rules.rule: After any multi-change fix where the bug works now, explicitly ablate the changes that are not obviously load-bearing.

rules.quote: If you can't ablate (e.g., destructive/hard-to-revert), say so explicitly in the report: "Cannot rule out [other change] as the actual fix."
rules.rule: If you cannot ablate a change (e.g., because it is destructive or hard to revert), say so explicitly in the report and state that the other change cannot be ruled out as the actual fix.

rules.quote: When committing a fix that depends on multiple changes, PROVE in the commit message which one is load-bearing (with ablation evidence) — not just which one you wrote last.
rules.rule: When committing a fix that depends on multiple changes, state in the commit message which change is load-bearing, supported by ablation evidence, rather than the change written last.

rules.quote: when ablation reveals a change was NOT needed, REMOVE it (don't keep "for diagnosability" unless you have a concrete future use case).
rules.rule: When ablation shows a change was not needed, remove it rather than keeping it, unless there is a concrete future use case for it.

rules.quote: replace **every non-alphanumeric character** (except existing dashes) with `-`
rules.rule: When deriving the Claude Code project directory key from an absolute path, replace every non-alphanumeric character, except existing dashes, with `-`, not just forward slashes.

rules.quote: `path.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9-]/g, '-')`
rules.rule: When computing the Claude Code project directory key from a path, use path.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9-]/g, '-').

rules.quote: use the `[^a-zA-Z0-9-]` regex
rules.rule: When writing code that reads from ~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/, use the regex [^a-zA-Z0-9-] to derive the project key.

rules.quote: never just `/`
rules.rule: When writing code that reads from ~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/, never derive the project key by replacing only forward slashes.

rules.quote: first check that the computed path matches what Claude Code actually uses
rules.rule: When debugging symptoms of AutoMemory importing 0 entries, first check that the computed memory path matches the directory Claude Code actually uses.

rules.quote: Always compare `resolveAutoMemoryDir(process.cwd())` output against `ls ~/.claude/projects/`
rules.rule: Always compare the output of resolveAutoMemoryDir(process.cwd()) against the listing of ~/.claude/projects/.

rules.quote: the four-axis mapping must be explicit and unambiguous
rules.rule: For every L3 (ruflo) hook handler and every learning-cycle step, state an explicit and unambiguous four-axis mapping (phase, loop, tier, upstream symbol).

rules.quote: one of `CAPTURE`, `RETRIEVE`, `APPLY`, `JUDGE`, `DISTILL`, `STORE`, `REINFORCE`, `FORGET`.
rules.rule: Assign each hook handler and learning-cycle step a phase from this set: CAPTURE, RETRIEVE, APPLY, JUDGE, DISTILL, STORE, REINFORCE, FORGET.

rules.quote: which temporal cadence runs it:
rules.rule: Assign each hook handler a loop: A (per inference, under 10ms), B (background, about every 30s), or C (session-end).

rules.quote: which serving tier handles it (for phases 1–3 only)
rules.rule: For handlers in phases 1–3, assign a serving tier: reactive, adaptive, or deliberative.

rules.quote: Phases 4–8 are not tier-routed
rules.rule: Do not assign a serving tier to handlers in phases 4–8.

rules.quote: with a gitnexus-verified `file:line` from the upstream source tree
rules.rule: Each hook handler's upstream symbol must be an exact function or class with a gitnexus-verified file:line from the upstream source tree.

rules.quote: Not a stub, not a placeholder, not a wrapper that reinvents the behaviour.
rules.rule: Do not use a stub, placeholder, or wrapper that reinvents upstream behaviour as a hook handler's upstream symbol.

rules.quote: No hook fires without that full mapping.
rules.rule: Do not let a hook fire unless its full four-axis mapping is defined.

rules.quote: No phase is "canonical" until upstream is verified.
rules.rule: Do not label a phase as canonical until its upstream implementation is verified.

rules.quote: fill in the 4-axis mapping (phase, loop, tier, upstream `file:line`)
rules.rule: Before adding a new hook handler, fill in its four-axis mapping (phase, loop, tier, upstream file:line).

rules.quote: cite it in the code comment
rules.rule: Cite a new hook handler's four-axis mapping in its code comment.

rules.quote: If any axis is unknown, the code doesn't land
rules.rule: If any axis of a hook handler's mapping is unknown, do not land the code.

rules.quote: resolve it via the §2 protocol in ADR-000-DDD first
rules.rule: Resolve any unknown mapping axis via the §2 protocol in ADR-000-DDD before landing the code.

rules.quote: confirm its mapping is still valid against the current upstream
rules.rule: When modifying an existing hook handler, confirm its mapping is still valid against the current upstream.

rules.quote: re-verify via gitnexus on each touch
rules.rule: Re-verify a hook handler's upstream file:line via gitnexus on each touch.

rules.quote: reject any handler that can't trace all four axes in under 10 seconds of reading
rules.rule: When reviewing code, reject any hook handler whose four axes cannot be traced in under 10 seconds of reading.

rules.quote: ask the catalog / pi-brain / upstream source before inventing a bypass
rules.rule: When upstream lacks a function for a phase, consult the catalog, pi-brain, or upstream source before inventing a bypass.

rules.quote: Every scoped ADR (001, 002, …) that touches a phase must update or cite that table.
rules.rule: Every scoped ADR that touches a phase must update or cite the canonical phase table in doc/adr/000-DDD.md §3.4.

rules.quote: you MUST restart the daemon for the change to take effect
rules.rule: After patching a JavaScript file loaded by a long-running daemon, restart that daemon so the change takes effect, since writing the file to disk is not enough.

rules.quote: must follow up with either:
rules.rule: After editing a daemon-resident file, follow up with either a full /exit and Claude Code restart, or `bash .claude/helpers/daemon-manager.sh restart`.

rules.quote: Edit a hook script → no restart needed
rules.rule: After editing a hook script, do not restart any daemon, because the next hook invocation will pick up the change.

rules.quote: Compare daemon start time (from `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=`) with file mtime (from `stat -c %y <file>`)
rules.rule: To check whether a running daemon has stale code, compare the daemon's start time from `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=` with the file's mtime from `stat -c %y <file>`.

rules.quote: Never ask the operator technical/design questions.
rules.rule: Never ask the operator technical or design questions; instead analyze the surface (code, memory, precedents, docs) and decide the best option yourself.

rules.quote: Analyze the surface (code, memory, precedents, docs) and decide the best option yourself.
rules.rule: When faced with a technical or design choice, analyze the surface (code, memory, precedents, docs) and decide the best option yourself.

rules.quote: Report the decision + reasoning in the update, not as a question.
rules.rule: Report technical decisions and their reasoning in the update, not as a question to the operator.

rules.quote: fix the impacted/related code in the SAME scope/commit — do not postpone "cleanup" or "swap targets" to a future pass.
rules.rule: When a change modifies existing behavior, contracts, or files, fix the impacted or related code in the same scope/commit; do not postpone cleanup or target swaps to a future pass.

rules.quote: If a newly-added Cargo dep obsoletes a workaround, replace the workaround now.
rules.rule: When a newly added Cargo dependency makes an existing workaround obsolete, replace the workaround in the same change.

rules.quote: If a renamed symbol breaks callers (gitnexus_impact shows d=1), fix the callers in the same commit.
rules.rule: When a renamed symbol breaks callers, fix the callers in the same commit.

rules.quote: If a new env var needs README update, do it now.
rules.rule: When a new environment variable needs a README update, update the README in the same change.

rules.quote: Don't leave `// TODO swap once deps land`.
rules.rule: Do not leave TODO comments deferring a workaround swap until dependencies land; update the code in the same integration commit.

rules.quote: When a path truly cannot compile, report + halt.
rules.rule: When a path truly cannot compile, report the blocker and halt rather than proceeding.

rules.quote: use GitNexus MCP tools FIRST
rules.rule: For questions about code ownership, call chains, cross-repo patterns, upstream divergence, or who calls what, use GitNexus MCP tools before grep or find.

rules.quote: Only fall back to grep/Read for
rules.rule: Fall back to grep or Read for code investigation only when the target is a .mjs local helper that is not deeply indexed, a file not in any indexed repo, or when the literal source text is needed instead of the graph.

rules.quote: load via `ToolSearch({query: "gitnexus query context"})`
rules.rule: Load the deferred GitNexus tools via ToolSearch before calling them.

rules.quote: memorize their use cases
rules.rule: Memorize the use cases of the primary GitNexus tools (list_repos, query, context, impact, xref).

rules.quote: Always specify `repo:` param
rules.rule: Always specify the repo parameter when calling GitNexus tools, since multiple repos are indexed.

rules.quote: Refresh after commits — run `npx gitnexus analyze`
rules.rule: Run npx gitnexus analyze to refresh the GitNexus graph after commits.

rules.quote: For local helpers, fall back to Read.
rules.rule: For local .mjs helpers whose symbols GitNexus cannot resolve, use Read instead of GitNexus context().

rules.quote: Claude Code hooks are a *data-source* for upstream self-learning, **not** the learning system itself.
rules.rule: Do not treat Claude Code hooks as the self-learning system; they are only a data source that feeds events to upstream.

rules.quote: translate Claude-Code JSON → event;
rules.rule: In the L3 layer, translate Claude Code hook JSON into an event.

rules.quote: run scope-survivor concerns (pre-bash regex, prompt cleaning)
rules.rule: In the L3 layer, run the scope-survivor concerns (pre-bash regex and prompt cleaning).

rules.quote: feed the event to an upstream orchestrator
rules.rule: In the L3 layer, feed each event to an upstream orchestrator.

rules.quote: render what it emits
rules.rule: In the L3 layer, render what the upstream orchestrator emits.

rules.quote: write local export artefacts
rules.rule: In the L3 layer, write local export artefacts.

rules.quote: Target ~180 LOC total.
rules.rule: Aim for the v4 L3 implementation to total about 180 lines of code.

rules.quote: is a MAP of what upstream does internally — not a TODO list of things to wire
rules.rule: Treat the §3.4 phase matrix as a map of upstream internals, not as a checklist of phases to wire up.

rules.quote: The single substrate call for Loop B/C background learning is `SonaEngine.tick()`
rules.rule: Use SonaEngine.tick() as the single substrate call for Loop B/C background learning.

rules.quote: NOT event-driven from `SessionEnd` / `Stop`
rules.rule: Do not trigger consolidation from SessionEnd or Stop events.

rules.quote: If that question has no answer, only THEN consider L3 wiring.
rules.rule: Before wiring anything at L3, check whether an IntelligenceEngine, NeuralSubstrate, or SonaEngine method exposes it; consider L3 wiring only if none does.

rules.quote: Refuse to wire phases upstream owns.
rules.rule: Do not wire phases that upstream owns.

rules.quote: If a new IPC command in ruvector-daemon.mjs is named after one of them, reject it as invention.
rules.rule: Reject any new IPC command in ruvector-daemon.mjs named after FORGET, PRUNE, CONSOLIDATE, DISTILL, or JUDGE as invention.

rules.quote: Measure daemon LOC as debt.
rules.rule: Track daemon lines of code as technical debt.

rules.quote: Publish it alongside KPIs.
rules.rule: Publish the daemon LOC metric alongside the KPIs.

rules.quote: `file:line` citations are delegation evidence, not wire-permission.
rules.rule: Do not treat file:line citations to upstream code as permission to expose and call that code from hooks.

rules.quote: Vendor overlays (`vendor/*.node`) are regression signals.
rules.rule: Treat vendor overlays (vendor/*.node) as regression signals.

rules.quote: Goal: empty `vendor/` after proper adoption.
rules.rule: Aim to empty the vendor/ directory after proper upstream adoption.

rules.quote: Don't schedule consolidation from hooks.
rules.rule: Do not schedule consolidation from hooks.

rules.quote: No `forceLearn`, no `session_end`, no `consolidate`, no `prune`, no `forget`.
rules.rule: Do not call forceLearn, session_end, consolidate, prune, or forget in the orchestration loop.

rules.quote: Never patch an MCP call, SQL query, or hook path based on a single-shot latency measurement.
rules.rule: Never patch an MCP call, SQL query, or hook path based on a single-shot latency measurement.

rules.quote: Always collect ≥10 samples, drop the first 2 as warmup, and report p50 (median) — not average or worst-case.
rules.rule: When measuring latency for a performance decision, collect at least 10 samples, drop the first 2 as warmup, and report p50 (median), not average or worst-case.

rules.quote: Before proposing a performance patch, measure with this node snippet:
rules.rule: Before proposing a performance patch, measure latency using the provided node snippet.

rules.quote: // Run ≥10 iterations, drop first 2, sort, take middle = p50
rules.rule: When running the latency snippet, run at least 10 iterations, drop the first 2, sort the results, and take the middle value as p50.

rules.quote: The daemon MUST use the napi_simple API:
rules.rule: When writing SONA daemon code, use the napi_simple API, not the napi.rs TrajectoryBuilder API.

rules.quote: `sona.beginTrajectory(embedding)` → returns `u32` (NOT TrajectoryBuilder)
rules.rule: Call sona.beginTrajectory(embedding) in SONA daemon code and treat its return value as a u32 trajectory ID, not a TrajectoryBuilder.

rules.quote: `sona.addTrajectoryStep(id, activations, attention, reward)` (NOT `builder.addStep()`)
rules.rule: Add trajectory steps in SONA daemon code with sona.addTrajectoryStep(id, activations, attention, reward), not builder.addStep().

rules.quote: `sona.endTrajectory(id, quality)` (NOT `sona.endTrajectory(builder, quality)`)
rules.rule: End trajectories in SONA daemon code with sona.endTrajectory(id, quality), passing the integer ID rather than a builder object.

rules.quote: Before writing SONA daemon code, check `lib.rs` to see which NAPI module is compiled.
rules.rule: Before writing SONA daemon code, check lib.rs to confirm which NAPI module is compiled.

rules.quote: Use GitNexus `context({name: "SonaEngine", file_path: "crates/sona/src/napi_simple.rs"})` to see the actual API.
rules.rule: To see the actual SONA NAPI API, call GitNexus context({name: "SonaEngine", file_path: "crates/sona/src/napi_simple.rs"}).

rules.quote: ALWAYS show the fallback level and quality percentage for each layer FIRST
rules.rule: When analysing a system with graceful degradation, show the fallback level and quality percentage for each layer before any other metrics.

rules.quote: Speed, uptime, and "it returns JSON" are secondary.
rules.rule: When reporting a system's status, do not lead with speed, uptime, or whether it returns data; report those after layer quality.

rules.quote: show `advertised tier → actual tier → fallback tier → quality %`
rules.rule: For every layer of a system being analysed, show its advertised tier, actual tier, fallback tier, and quality percentage, in that order.

rules.quote: If quality is 0% or degenerate, say so BEFORE reporting speed
rules.rule: If a layer's quality is 0% or degenerate, state that before reporting its speed.

rules.quote: If a system "reports" features it crashed loading, flag the misleading report
rules.rule: If a system reports features that failed to load, flag that report as misleading.

rules.quote: If confidence is flat across all inputs, that IS the quality signal
rules.rule: If a confidence value is the same across all inputs, treat that constancy as a quality signal.

rules.quote: don't present it as "high confidence"
rules.rule: Do not present a confidence value that is flat across all inputs as high confidence.

rules.quote: Lead with "fast at returning garbage" when that's the truth
rules.rule: When a system is fast but returns poor-quality output, lead the report with that fact.

rules.quote: Ruflo v4 must NOT include `/mnt/data/dev/ruvector_brain_src/` or `/home/jordi/.ruvector/pi-brain/` as Cargo path dependencies.
rules.rule: Do not add `/mnt/data/dev/ruvector_brain_src/` or `/home/jordi/.ruvector/pi-brain/` as Cargo path dependencies in Ruflo v4.

rules.quote: Do NOT uncomment `ruvllm = { path = ... }` / `sona = { path = ... }` / `ruvector-* = { path = ... }` in `crates/ruvflo-ruvllm-ext/Cargo.toml`.
rules.rule: Do not uncomment the ruvllm, sona, or ruvector-* path dependencies in `crates/ruvflo-ruvllm-ext/Cargo.toml`.

rules.quote: Runtime NAPI must come from the PUBLISHED `@ruvflo/ruvllm-ext` npm package
rules.rule: Source the runtime NAPI from the published `@ruvflo/ruvllm-ext` npm package.

rules.quote: Any new NAPI surface that requires sona/ruvllm crates directly (e.g. `JsLoopCoordinator` wrapping `sona::LoopCoordinator`) is BLOCKED until this deferral lifts
rules.rule: Do not add any new NAPI surface that requires the sona or ruvllm crates directly until the deferral is lifted.

rules.quote: document in `doc/adr/002-ruvector-brain-deferred.md`
rules.rule: Document the blocked NAPI surface in `doc/adr/002-ruvector-brain-deferred.md`.

rules.quote: mark the stubs clearly
rules.rule: Mark any blocked NAPI stubs clearly.

rules.quote: `JsReasoningBank` (store/consolidate/stats — plus `search` + `default()` once published), `JsVerdictAnalyzer`, `JsPatternConsolidator`, `JsQualityScoring`, `JsPattern::fromTrajectory` (if the published npm exposes it).
rules.rule: Deliver the capabilities JsReasoningBank, JsVerdictAnalyzer, JsPatternConsolidator, JsQualityScoring, and JsPattern::fromTrajectory (if the published npm exposes it) via the published NAPI package.

rules.quote: must NOT be included in ruflo architecture guides, integration proposals, or dependency maps
rules.rule: Do not include RVF (RuVector Format, including cognitive containers, MicroVm, RvfStore, EbpfCompiler/EbpfManager, .rvf files, and eBPF symbols) in ruflo architecture guides, integration proposals, or dependency maps.

rules.quote: Don't mention RVF, MicroVm, RvfStore, or eBPF-in-RVF symbols in Phase 3 / Phase 4 / Phase 5 proposals for ruflo
rules.rule: Do not mention RVF, MicroVm, RvfStore, or eBPF-in-RVF symbols in Phase 3, Phase 4, or Phase 5 proposals for ruflo.

rules.quote: When pulling foxRef content (Part01 L58–105, L233, Part02 L227–238, L661, L673), filter RVF sections out
rules.rule: When pulling foxRef content from the specified line ranges, filter out RVF sections.

rules.quote: Witness chains / SHAKE-256 can still be referenced when they come from `prime-radiant::WitnessSource`
rules.rule: Witness chains and SHAKE-256 may be referenced when they come from prime-radiant::WitnessSource.

rules.quote: π brain memories about RVF (e.g., *"RVF Cognitive Container - Sealed WASM Container"*) are informational only, not architecture we adopt
rules.rule: Treat π brain memories about RVF as informational only, and do not adopt them as architecture.

rules.quote: Patch `ruvector/dist/core/onnx-embedder.js` exports before creating AdaptiveEmbedder:
rules.rule: Before creating AdaptiveEmbedder, patch the exports of ruvector/dist/core/onnx-embedder.js to use the @xenova/transformers pipeline instead of the missing bundled ONNX WASM files.

rules.quote: Load `@xenova/transformers` pipeline (model cached at `@xenova/transformers/.cache/`)
rules.rule: Load the @xenova/transformers pipeline when patching the ONNX embedder, using the model cached at @xenova/transformers/.cache/.

rules.quote: Override `isOnnxAvailable`, `initOnnxEmbedder`, `embed`, `embedBatch`
rules.rule: When patching the ONNX embedder, override the isOnnxAvailable, initOnnxEmbedder, embed, and embedBatch functions.

rules.quote: Verify: embed('test') returns >50% non-zero values (dense = real ONNX, sparse = hash poison)
rules.rule: Verify the patched embedder by checking that embed('test') returns more than 50% non-zero values, and treat sparse output as hash poison rather than real ONNX.

rules.quote: Always verify daemon logs show "real ONNX confirmed" not "hash fallback".
rules.rule: Always verify that daemon logs show "real ONNX confirmed" rather than "hash fallback".

rules.quote: If sparse, the learning is garbage.
rules.rule: If embeddings are sparse, do not trust the resulting learning, since it is garbage.

rules.quote: NEVER write SQL directly from hook scripts
rules.rule: Never write SQL directly from any hook script; hook scripts must not write to the database themselves.

rules.quote: NEVER open memory.db from node -e debug scripts while MCP server is running.
rules.rule: Never open memory.db from node -e debug scripts while the MCP server is running.

rules.quote: NEVER be the "third writer"
rules.rule: Never act as an additional writer to memory.db when the MCP server owns the database.

rules.quote: if the MCP server owns the DB, ALL access goes through MCP.
rules.rule: When the MCP server owns the database, route all database access through MCP tools.

rules.quote: Hook files: ALL data writes go through `callMcp()` to MCP tools
rules.rule: In hook files, send all data writes through callMcp() to MCP tools.

rules.quote: Only exception: `hook-bridge.cjs` stale cleanup at SessionStart (runs BEFORE MCP starts, inside transaction)
rules.rule: The only permitted direct database write from a hook is stale cleanup in hook-bridge.cjs at SessionStart, which runs before the MCP server starts and inside a transaction.

rules.quote: Debug queries: use MCP tools, or STOP the MCP server first, then query, then restart
rules.rule: For debug queries against memory.db, use MCP tools, or stop the MCP server first, query, then restart it.

rules.quote: If you need to inspect memory.db: `callMcp('hooks_intelligence', {})` or similar MCP tool
rules.rule: To inspect memory.db, call an MCP tool such as callMcp('hooks_intelligence', {}) rather than querying the database directly.

rules.quote: NEVER `require('better-sqlite3')`
rules.rule: Never require better-sqlite3 to inspect or access memory.db.

rules.quote: **The rule: 1 WRITER. Always. No exceptions.**
rules.rule: Only one writer may access memory.db at any time, always, with no exceptions.

rules.quote: every call that crosses a boundary (I/O, IPC, upstream library, filesystem, network) MUST be wrapped in try/catch whose catch branch writes the error to a centralized log file
rules.rule: In daemons, MCP servers, and hooks, wrap every call that crosses a boundary (I/O, IPC, upstream library, filesystem, network) in try/catch, and have the catch branch write the error to a centralized log file.

rules.quote: Silent failure is prohibited.
rules.rule: Never let a failure at a runtime boundary in daemons, MCP servers, or hooks fail silently.

rules.quote: propagate a structured error value (e.g. `{ ok: false, error: msg }` for IPC) rather than throwing raw
rules.rule: When a function cannot continue after a boundary error, return a structured error value (e.g. `{ ok: false, error: msg }` for IPC) instead of throwing the raw error.

rules.quote: if it can continue with partial data (observability endpoints), return the partial data plus an error field.
rules.rule: When an observability endpoint can continue with partial data after an error, return the partial data plus an error field.

rules.quote: wrap internal data collection so a partial-broken sub-component returns a partial response with an error field rather than crashing the whole ping. Acceptable.
rules.rule: In observability endpoints, wrap internal data collection so a broken sub-component returns a partial response with an error field instead of crashing the whole ping.

rules.quote: wrap each resource's shutdown independently so one failure does not block the others.
rules.rule: In lifecycle cleanup (session_end, SIGTERM handlers), wrap each resource's shutdown independently so one failure does not block the others.

rules.quote: wrap so an unavailable daemon is logged rather than silently breaking the session.
rules.rule: In spawn and daemon-start paths, wrap the code so an unavailable daemon is logged rather than silently breaking the session.

rules.quote: Use the direct call; let try/catch capture any real fault.
rules.rule: Call contract-guaranteed upstream methods directly and do not guard them with typeof checks; let try/catch capture any real fault.

rules.quote: Silent fallbacks like `return null` or `return {}` without logging.
rules.rule: Do not return null or {} as a silent fallback without logging the error.

rules.quote: If you catch, you LOG. Period.
rules.rule: Whenever you catch an error, log it.

rules.quote: Swallowing errors so tests pass.
rules.rule: Do not swallow errors just to make tests pass.

rules.quote: If an error appears in test output, fix the root cause.
rules.rule: When an error appears in test output, fix its root cause rather than hiding it.

rules.quote: Introducing ad-hoc sentinel values (e.g. `-1`, `'error'`) as "was-this-ok" flags.
rules.rule: Do not introduce ad-hoc sentinel values (e.g. -1 or 'error') as was-this-ok flags.

rules.quote: Return `{ok: false, error: msg}` or equivalent structured form.
rules.rule: Signal success or failure with a structured form such as `{ok: false, error: msg}` rather than sentinel values.

rules.quote: catch blocks must not attempt to retry by opening a parallel writer.
rules.rule: Do not retry from a catch block by opening a parallel writer.

rules.quote: every wrapped boundary call still traces 4-axis (phase × loop × tier × upstream).
rules.rule: Map every wrapped boundary call to the 4-axis (phase × loop × tier × upstream) even though it is wrapped in try/catch.

rules.quote: It calls upstream directly and trusts the returned results exactly as they come.
rules.rule: Call upstream directly and trust its returned results exactly as they come, without transforming them.

rules.quote: Never synthesise formulas, aggregations, thresholds, or mappings that transform upstream's contract into something "nicer".
rules.rule: Never synthesise formulas, aggregations, thresholds, or mappings that transform upstream's output contract into something "nicer".

rules.quote: pass a **neutral default** and move on
rules.rule: When an upstream symbol requires an input the caller does not meaningfully possess, pass a neutral default and move on.

rules.quote: add a **detection log** if the returned shape is ever worth observing
rules.rule: Add a detection log when an upstream returned shape is worth observing.

rules.quote: Adding new upstream helpers (via local Rust rebuild + `#[napi]`) to paper over a missing convenience is ALSO invention
rules.rule: Do not add new upstream helpers (via local Rust rebuild + #[napi]) to paper over a missing convenience.

rules.quote: **USE WHAT UPSTREAM PROVIDES, as much as possible**
rules.rule: Use what upstream provides, as much as possible.

rules.quote: ADOPT IT
rules.rule: Adopt an upstream export when it improves the quality of what we have.

rules.quote: "we don't need it"
rules.rule: Do not reject an upstream export because "we don't need it".

rules.quote: "our use case is different"
rules.rule: Do not reject an upstream export because "our use case is different" without first checking whether it applies.

rules.quote: "it's a different domain"
rules.rule: Do not reject an upstream export because "it's a different domain"; check whether the domain composes with ours.

rules.quote: "too many knobs"
rules.rule: Do not reject an upstream export because of "too many knobs"; ignore the knobs you don't use and adopt what is load-bearing.

rules.quote: NEVER reject because "it's too much" or "we haven't used it before".
rules.rule: Never reject an upstream export because "it's too much" or "we haven't used it before".

rules.quote: We already have the exact same capability covered by another upstream path AND they can't meaningfully compose.
rules.rule: Skip an upstream export only if the exact same capability is already covered by another upstream path and the two cannot meaningfully compose.

rules.quote: The export's domain is **provably unrelated** to our use case
rules.rule: Skip an upstream export only when its domain is provably unrelated to our use case.

rules.quote: It's an internal primitive that a higher-level export already composes for us (transitively covered).
rules.rule: Skip an upstream export that is an internal primitive already composed by a higher-level export.

rules.quote: When in doubt: evaluate empirically — ablate with real data, observe returned values, decide based on evidence.
rules.rule: When in doubt about an upstream export, evaluate it empirically: ablate with real data, observe returned values, and decide based on evidence.

rules.quote: use everything upstream gives us, exactly as it gives it to us, without adding glue logic between.
rules.rule: Use everything upstream gives us exactly as it is given, without adding glue logic between.

rules.quote: y delegar en (creerse) upstream results, como llegan
rules.rule: Delegate to upstream and trust its results as they arrive.

rules.quote: Como MAXIMO, puedes añadir un fallback neutral junto con algun mecanismo/log que te permita detectar si hay problemas con upstream
rules.rule: At most, add a neutral fallback together with a mechanism or log that detects problems with upstream.

rules.quote: investigar el RootCause real y fixearlo
rules.rule: When an upstream result is unexpected, null, or empty, investigate the real root cause and fix it.

rules.quote: NO AÑADIR MAS funciones de UPSTREAM ocultas por debajo
rules.rule: Do not add more hidden upstream functions underneath to work around an unexpected upstream result.

rules.quote: If yes, do that.
rules.rule: Before proposing an adapter-layer change, if you can pass what you have directly to upstream, neutral-default the rest and do that.

rules.quote: Source-read.
rules.rule: When an upstream result is unexpected, read the upstream source to locate where it is computed.

rules.quote: Cite `file:line`.
rules.rule: Cite the upstream file:line where the unexpected result is computed.

rules.quote: the fix is upstream-only — not adapter-side synthesis
rules.rule: If the upstream logic causes the unexpected result, make the fix upstream-only, not adapter-side synthesis.

rules.quote: Legitimate: reading the correct upstream field name
rules.rule: Reading the correct upstream field name is a legitimate adapter-side fix.

rules.quote: Invention: computing a value upstream was supposed to provide.
rules.rule: Do not compute a value that upstream was supposed to provide.

rules.quote: Forbidden unless operator explicitly authorises it as a forcing-function closure
rules.rule: Do not add a new upstream wrapper (via rebuild + #[napi]) unless the operator explicitly authorises it as a forcing-function closure.

rules.quote: wrapping boundary calls in try/catch + logging returned anomalies is ALLOWED and ENCOURAGED
rules.rule: Wrap boundary calls in try/catch and log returned anomalies.

rules.quote: ablate it afterwards to confirm it's load-bearing
rules.rule: After adding adapter logic, ablate it to confirm it is load-bearing.

rules.quote: If not load-bearing, remove.
rules.rule: Remove adapter logic that is not load-bearing.

rules.quote: operator wants me to decide, not ask every technical question
rules.rule: Decide technical questions yourself rather than asking the operator about each one.

rules.quote: But "invent or not" is a scope/governance decision, worth confirming.
rules.rule: Confirm with the operator any decision about whether something counts as invention.

rules.quote: would upstream's author recognise this as a natural use of their API, or as me patching around their design?
rules.rule: Before proposing a change, ask whether upstream's author would recognise it as a natural use of their API or as a patch around their design.

rules.quote: If the latter, it's invention.
rules.rule: If a proposed change patches around upstream's design, treat it as invention and do not make it.

rules.quote: use `@ruvector/sona::SonaEngine` directly with externally-computed embeddings
rules.rule: In the v4 daemon, use @ruvector/sona::SonaEngine directly with externally computed embeddings.

rules.quote: Do NOT use `@ruvector/ruvllm::SonaCoordinator` for trajectory recording, extraction, or retrieval.
rules.rule: In the v4 daemon, do not use @ruvector/ruvllm::SonaCoordinator for trajectory recording, extraction, or retrieval.

rules.quote: Do NOT reimplement upstream logic in JS under any circumstance.
rules.rule: Never reimplement upstream logic in JavaScript, under any circumstance.

rules.quote: const sona = new SonaEngine(384);` — no config invention, no override.
rules.rule: Construct the engine as `new SonaEngine(384)` without inventing configuration or overriding defaults.

rules.quote: If upstream doesn't produce expected results with canonical calls, REPORT IT — do not patch around it.
rules.rule: If upstream does not produce expected results with canonical calls, report it; do not patch around it.

rules.quote: No bypass
rules.rule: Do not bypass upstream.

rules.quote: no threshold overrides
rules.rule: Do not override upstream thresholds.

rules.quote: no custom extraction
rules.rule: Do not write custom extraction logic in place of upstream extraction.

rules.quote: no concatenation heuristics
rules.rule: Do not use concatenation heuristics.

rules.quote: no confidence formulas
rules.rule: Do not invent confidence formulas.

rules.quote: no step-type regex
rules.rule: Do not use step-type regex.

rules.quote: Use Integer IDs (see `feedback_napi_simple.md`).
rules.rule: Use integer IDs for trajectories and steps when calling SonaEngine.

rules.quote: Arrays (not scalars) for activations/attention.
rules.rule: Pass activations and attention weights as arrays, not scalars.

rules.quote: Do NOT bypass upstream or reimplement extraction — supply raw vectors to upstream, let upstream do everything else.
rules.rule: Do not bypass upstream or reimplement extraction; supply raw vectors to upstream and let upstream do everything else.

rules.quote: Never add a `scripts/patches/NNN-PATCH-*.sh` for changes to `viz/`.
rules.rule: Never add a scripts/patches/NNN-PATCH-*.sh file for changes to the viz/ directory.

rules.quote: Viz is a separate add-on consumer, not part of the bootstrap pipeline.
rules.rule: Treat viz/ as a separate add-on consumer, not part of the bootstrap pipeline.

rules.quote: For viz changes: edit `viz/src/*.js` directly + commit.
rules.rule: For viz changes, edit viz/src/*.js files directly and commit them, without creating a patch file.

rules.quote: No patch file. No sentinel. No verify-v2 invariant.
rules.rule: For viz changes, do not create a patch file, sentinel, or verify-v2 invariant.

rules.quote: For bootstrap changes (daemon, hooks, MCP, helpers, settings, node_modules patches, etc.): use `scripts/patches/NNN-PATCH-*.sh` with sentinel + idempotency + drift anchor.
rules.rule: For bootstrap changes (daemon, hooks, MCP, helpers, settings, node_modules patches, etc.), implement them as scripts/patches/NNN-PATCH-*.sh files that include a sentinel, idempotency, and a drift anchor.

rules.quote: If a viz change is needed alongside a bootstrap change, ship them in separate commits (or one commit with two distinct stanzas)
rules.rule: When a viz change accompanies a bootstrap change, ship them in separate commits, or in one commit with two distinct stanzas.

rules.quote: but never via the patch pipeline for the viz part.
rules.rule: Never deliver the viz part of a combined change through the patch pipeline.

rules.quote: For viz binaries / static assets distribution to fresh clones: that's a build-system concern (npm install / git clone), not a bootstrap patch.
rules.rule: Handle distribution of viz binaries and static assets to fresh clones through the build system (npm install / git clone), not as a bootstrap patch.

rules.quote: changes go to scripts/, not .claude/
rules.rule: When making changes to this bootstrap kit project, put them in the scripts/ directory, not in .claude/.

rules.quote: Test in v202, sync back to portable part + docs.
rules.rule: Test changes by installing into a fresh project (such as v202) before considering them done.

rules.quote: Make changes in `scripts/` (the portable part)
rules.rule: Make all changes to the installer in the scripts/ directory (the portable part).

rules.quote: Test by installing into a fresh project (e.g., v202)
rules.rule: Test changes by installing into a fresh project such as v202 using the bootstrap script copied from scripts/.

rules.quote: Once verified, sync documentation (README.md, gap analysis)
rules.rule: Once changes are verified, update the documentation (README.md and the gap analysis) to match.

rules.quote: never edit it directly as the source of truth
rules.rule: Never edit .claude/helpers/ directly as the source of truth; update it only by re-running the bootstrap.

rules.quote: If it needs updating, re-run the bootstrap.
rules.rule: If .claude/helpers/ needs updating, update it by re-running the bootstrap script.

rules.quote: `node_modules/`, `.swarm/`, `.ruvector/` — runtime artifacts, not part of the kit.
rules.rule: Do not make changes to node_modules/, .swarm/, or .ruvector/ as part of the kit, since they are runtime artifacts.

rules.quote: check if `SonaEngine` / `IntelligenceEngine` already exposes the capability.
rules.rule: Before adding any new hook wiring, check whether SonaEngine or IntelligenceEngine already exposes the needed capability.

rules.quote: Read `sona/examples/` (3 files, ~200 LOC)
rules.rule: Before adding new hook wiring, read the sona/examples/ directory to see the full SonaEngine method surface.

rules.quote: if it's a phase name (consolidate/prune/distill/forget), reject as invention.
rules.rule: Reject any proposed new IPC command name that is a phase name (consolidate, prune, distill, forget) as invented orchestration.

rules.quote: Legitimate IPC commands: `observe`, `status`, maybe `export`.
rules.rule: Limit IPC commands to observe, status, and possibly export.

rules.quote: propose P1 (tick-driven daemon) as the first
rules.rule: When writing the ADR-009 candidate, propose P1 (tick-driven daemon) as the first 'delete wiring in favour of upstream call' ADR.

rules.quote: move ruvector-catalog from step 4 to step 1-2 of CLAUDE.md §2 research protocol.
rules.rule: Move ruvector-catalog to steps 1-2 of the CLAUDE.md §2 research protocol, ahead of foxref and pi-brain deep dives.

rules.quote: `setInterval(() => engine.tick(), 30_000)`
rules.rule: On daemon startup, call engine.tick() on a 30-second setInterval.

rules.quote: `endTrajectory(builder, quality)` only
rules.rule: In the Stop and SubagentStop hook-handler branches, call only endTrajectory(builder, quality).

rules.quote: drop `forceLearn: true` flag
rules.rule: Do not pass the forceLearn: true flag in the Stop and SubagentStop hook-handler branches.

rules.quote: drop `session_end` flush entirely
rules.rule: Do not perform a session_end flush.

rules.quote: on first-run detection of empty pattern store, walk git log + file structure
rules.rule: On first-run detection of an empty pattern store, walk the git log and file structure.

rules.quote: synthesize trajectories (`beginTrajectory/addStep/endTrajectory`)
rules.rule: Synthesize trajectories using beginTrajectory, addStep, and endTrajectory.

rules.quote: then let `tick()` crystallise via Loop B
rules.rule: After synthesizing trajectories, let tick() crystallise patterns via Loop B.

rules.quote: inspect `ruvector/npm/packages/ruvector/bin/cli.js` for the signal-extraction algorithm before implementing
rules.rule: Before implementing the cold-start pretrain, inspect ruvector/npm/packages/ruvector/bin/cli.js for the signal-extraction algorithm.

rules.quote: read in this order when designing upstream adoption
rules.rule: When designing upstream adoption, read the four ruvector upstream references in the order listed in the file.

rules.quote: do not adopt the engine choice
rules.rule: Do not adopt the Q-learning engine/RvLite choice from ruvector's HOOKS.md; take only its CLI surface and concepts.

rules.quote: **Use when:** designing daemon IPC surface, adopting Tier-1, answering "what's the single substrate call for X?"
rules.rule: Consult the ruvector sona/examples/ canonical SonaEngine usage when designing a daemon IPC surface, adopting Tier-1, or answering "what's the single substrate call for X?".

rules.quote: **Use when:** building user-facing CLI surface, designing cold-start bootstrap, adding self-healing diagnostics.
rules.rule: Consult ruvector's HOOKS.md when building a user-facing CLI surface, designing a cold-start bootstrap, or adding self-healing diagnostics.

rules.quote: Implementation to inspect for pretrain algorithm:
rules.rule: When investigating the pretrain algorithm, inspect ruvector/npm/packages/ruvector/bin/cli.js.

rules.quote: **Use when:** questioning whether a given orchestration belongs in hooks or in the daemon's main loop.
rules.rule: Consult agent-coordinator.ts when questioning whether a given orchestration belongs in hooks or in the daemon's main loop.

rules.quote: Default from this reference: main loop, not hooks.
rules.rule: When deciding whether an orchestration belongs in hooks or in the daemon's main loop, default to the main loop, not hooks.

rules.quote: **Use when:** designing a ruvector consumer, answering capability-mapping questions, running §2 research.
rules.rule: Consult the ruvector catalog's own src/catalog/ and SKILL.md when designing a ruvector consumer, answering capability-mapping questions, or running §2 research.

rules.quote: `bun src/cli.ts search "<query>"` from catalog root, OR read `SKILL.md`
rules.rule: To access the ruvector catalog, run `bun src/cli.ts search "<query>"` from the catalog root, or read SKILL.md and src/catalog/data-cap-defaults.ts directly.

rules.quote: promote to step 1-2
rules.rule: Move the ruvector-catalog check in the CLAUDE.md §2 research protocol from step 4 up to step 1-2.

rules.quote: Put it at the top of the research funnel when the question is concrete
rules.rule: When a research question is concrete ("which method?") rather than abstract ("which architecture?"), consult the ruvector catalog at the top of the research funnel.
